_note: Machine-readable form of the producer conformance rules. Enforced by tools/wire_spec_lint.py, which is dependency-free and meant to be copied by consumers; this generator only resolves the 'decided_at' provenance below. Each rule is exercised by negatives/<rule>.json, and generation fails if a linter predicate stops firing on its negative or if a cited symbol disappears. 'needs' lists the rules this one cannot be judged without; a rule that needs another is reported in 'undecidable', never silently passed.

rules.rule: every @graph entity declares a non-empty string @id

rules.consequence: validation does NOT catch this: dereferencing returns the first match and the shadowed entity is silently lost

rules.rule: a root dataset with @id './' exists and declares mainEntity
mainEntity resolves to an entity that exists in @graph

rules.consequence: a bare string passes validation but crashes the parser; an array crashes both
rules.rule: the workflow declares programmingLanguage as an object with @id

rules.consequence: validation requires the key but not that it be non-empty; an empty value yields vre_type 'unknown' downstream
rules.rule: programmingLanguage resolves to an entity with a non-empty identifier

rules.consequence: a missing hasPart raises TypeError deep in the parser, with no useful message
rules.rule: root dataset declares hasPart (an empty list is legal)

rules.consequence: hasPart is the ONLY enumeration source for files; a File entity absent from it is invisible to consumers. RocrateBuilder never emits this shape, but the TOSCA-authored galaxy_tosca_stage fixture does, so the rule is about hand-authored producers
rules.rule: every File entity appears in root hasPart

rules.consequence: VREPayload.input_files excludes the descriptor by @id, so a colliding file is dropped from the data files. A crate cannot make this mistake without ALSO duplicating an @id, so W002 always fires alongside it
rules.rule: no File entity shares its @id with the workflow

rules.consequence: this library copies FileInput.checksum verbatim and does not check its shape, so a truncated or non-hex digest is published as-is and only fails a consumer that verifies it
rules.rule: a sha256 property, when present, is a 64-character lowercase hex digest

rules.consequence: unresolvable references are skipped, so the slot silently never exists for the consumer. Note that an inline FormalParameter object is NOT a substitute for a graph entity: only its @id is read, and the entity with that @id supplies every property, so inline properties are ignored
rules.rule: every reference in workflow.input and workflow.output resolves to an entity in @graph

rules.consequence: consumers cannot detect a payload shape change
rules.rule: the root descriptor declares the wire format profile

rules.consequence: the parse path iterates these values directly, so a single object instead of a one-element array iterates its members and yields nothing: the slot list or file list comes back EMPTY with no exception and no other rule firing. Serialisers that omit the wrapper for a lone element are common, which makes this the cheapest way to lose a whole payload section in a non-Python producer
rules.rule: every hasPart, input and output value is a list, even with exactly one element

rules.consequence: parsing/infrastructure.py reads @type off the entry itself and never dereferences a reference, so a reference logs "Input is not of type File, skipping." and the input file silently does not exist in RuntimePlatform.input_files
rules.rule: INFRASTRUCTURE PROFILE ONLY: each entry in a RuntimePlatform's input array is a full inline entity carrying @type "File", not a "{"@id": "..."}" reference to one
